bc_werbworld.blurb: Werbworld is a small overhanging crag among the eastern outliers at Skaha Bluffs, above Skaha Lake near Penticton. It has six sport routes, five of them in the 5.11 range and one at 5.12, so it suits climbers who already lead hard and want steep, powerful pulls on big holds rather than slab or easy mileage. It is the first overhung wall you meet on the way out from the upper lot, which makes it a quick detour. Expect few other parties compared with the main walls, since these outlying crags see lighter traffic.
bc_werbworld.approach: From the trail just below the upper lot, walk past Daycare and continue east along the path as it winds back toward the crags on the left. The first overhung rock you reach is this one.

bc_the_egg.blurb: The Egg is a single boulder on a small bench above Arrow Lake in the West Kootenay, part of the Predator Ridge bouldering zone near Castlegar. It holds six problems running from V1 up to V5, with two easy-to-moderate pairs at the low end and a pair of harder lines at the top. The gneiss here is compact with mostly sloping holds, a different feel from the rest of Predator Ridge. It sits a short way along a trail fork past the Wizard Cow boulders, so it pairs well with a session at its neighbours.

bc_atlantis.blurb: Atlantis is a set of lakeshore gneiss boulders in the Beachside zone of the Arrow Lake bouldering, in the West Kootenay near Castlegar. It has six problems from V1 to V5, mostly V2 to V4, and a few sit right on sandy beach. Because the boulders lie low next to the water, they are submerged in high-water months and only come into condition when the reservoir drops. Plan around the lake level and check it before making the drive; you reach the boulders by heading to the lake side of the Low Tide boulders.

bc_the_stained_walls.blurb: The Stained Walls is a broad, mostly undeveloped band of cliffs at Harrison Bluffs in the Fraser Valley, stretching west from the top of Tree Frog toward Falcon Crest. It has six routes, five of them trad and one sport. Grades span from 5.5 up to 5.11, with three at 5.10, so there is something for newer leaders and for those wanting a harder test. The bluffs as a whole get morning to midday sun, and the low elevation makes sunny winter days workable.

bc_mount_shadowfax.blurb: Mount Shadowfax is a 2,315 m summit in the Tolkien Range of the Coast Mountains, north of Pemberton, rising steeply above Phelix Creek. The easiest way up is a short, steep hike with a little scrambling, so most visitors treat it as a day outing. Technical lines are fewer: there are six routes, mostly trad at 5.9 to 5.11, plus one aid line and one mixed line. This is remote alpine terrain, with a snow-free window that centres on the height of summer.
